name: Discoball
description: A cool, mysterious woman in her early thirties who sings French house at a desert arts festival, her whole head hidden inside a mirrored disco-ball helmet.
build: A tall slender adult build of ordinary proportions: straight shoulders, a slim torso, long arms and legs of ordinary length, standing upright with straight knees.
face: Her face is fully hidden inside an opaque spherical helmet only slightly wider than a head, covered in a grid of large bold square silver mirror tiles about an inch across, reflecting pale blue-white highlights; light-brown skin shows at the neck and hands.
hair: No hair visible; the mirror-ball helmet covers the whole head down to the jaw line.
outfit: A sleek black long-sleeved turtleneck jumpsuit, fitted, the sleeves ending at the wrists so both hands are bare; a wide silver metallic belt at the waist; a short cropped white faux-fur jacket ending at the ribs, sleeves to the elbows; black ankle boots with chunky heels.
performance_style: Cool and still: feet hip-width, weight on one hip. The character-right hand rests open on the belt, the character-left arm bent with the open hand at shoulder height, palm forward, fingers spread and fully visible. The mirror-ball head held level and square to the front.
location: A sound camp dance floor on the playa at night: a low wooden deck running to the bottom of the frame, a tall steel truss with a big speaker stack behind, strings of blue and white lights overhead, and a dark starry sky.
recognition_cues: a spherical mirror-ball helmet of large silver tiles hiding the whole head
a sleek black jumpsuit with a wide silver belt
avoid: a visible face, eyes or mouth
a helmet much wider than the shoulders

sing.intent: French-house vocal loop: her face is hidden, so the head and body carry the singing — bring the mic in the character-right hand up to the mirror-ball helmet where the mouth would be, bob the helmet forward and back on every beat and tilt it on the long phrase, roll the shoulders, sweep the character-left open hand out on the filter drop, then lower the mic and return to the cool stance. The helmet stays a smooth mirror ball throughout. The mouth must visibly open and change shape across the loop so she unmistakably reads as singing.

animations.flinch: Brief surprise at a loud blast from a passing sound system: the shoulders lift, the torso draws back and both open hands rise to chest height, then she settles back to her stance. No opponent, strike or physical contact.
animations.guard: One-shot stage self-protection against a gust of playa dust: step the feet wider, bring the character-left forearm across in front of the face with the character-right hand open at the hip, then hold a steady grounded finish. Not combat.
animations.entrance: One-shot entrance: glide in with slow smooth steps, the mirror-ball head level, turn square to the front, then land in her opening stance with both open hands in full view.
animations.victory: One-shot finish: snap both hands up in a wide V, tip the mirror-ball helmet back toward the sky, pop one hip, then hold a cool triumphant pose.
animations.ko: Non-contact performance defeat: she stays on her feet while the cool fades — the shoulders slump, both open hands hang limp at her sides, and the mirror-ball helmet tips heavily forward toward the ground. She holds a standing, visibly deflated finish. She remains standing on both feet in every frame — no kneeling, crouching, sitting, sinking, or going to the ground. Do not imply impact, injury, or an opponent.
